Daily GGR Trend — Sep 14–20
Executive Summary

For the week of Sep 14–20, 2026, Banana Craze generated ₱3,467,469.00 in settled bet amount from 9,535 users across 647,219 settled rounds, landing at ₱105,780.88 GGR — a positive house result — with blended RTP at 96.95%.

  • Best day: Thursday, Sep 17 — ₱37,743.50 GGR on ₱757,045.50 wagered (95.01% RTP).
  • Weakest day: Monday, Sep 14 — GGR dipped to −₱18,383.75 on ₱230,435.00 wagered, at 107.98% RTP.
  • 8,915 players (93.5% of the 9,535-user base) were new to Banana Craze this period (BANANA CRAZE Only New Players).
  • 63.68% of players who reached 20 rounds were net-negative at that point.
  • Round-survival drops sharply after round 20 (58.46% retained) and again after round 50 (30.87% retained) — see the Player Analysis page for the full churn curve.

Per-Day Averages: Sep 14–20

Week 38 Read

  • Bet volume swings sharply by day: Sunday, Sep 20 drew the week's highest single-day bet volume — ₱760,186.00 (21.9% of the week's total) on 146,336 rounds — closing at 95.81% RTP (₱31,817.50 GGR).
  • Revenue quality: Daily RTP ranged from 95.01% (Sep 17) to 107.98% (Sep 14) this week — a 13.0-point spread — pointing to short-run variance rather than a steady house edge.
  • New-player intake: Daily new players (Game Engine-new, Lifecycle definition) ranged from 210 (Sep 16) to 2168 (Sep 17), averaging 1274/day across the week's 8,915 new players.
  • Busiest day: Friday, Sep 18 was the week's busiest day by rounds (161,945) and closed at ₱19,898.00 GGR (97.00% RTP).
  • Week-over-week: compared to the prior week (Sep 7–13), GGR moved from ₱45,448.75 to ₱105,780.88 on bet volume of ₱763,385.00 to ₱3,467,469.00 (94.05% to 96.95% RTP).

Daily Drill-Down — Sep 14–207 days
  • The week is on target; single days are noise. RTP closed at 96.95% against the 97% design target — 0.05 pp off — but daily RTP ran 95.01% to 107.98% (σ 4.25 pp). Manage against the weekly close, not any one day.
  • 2026-09-14 was the only loss day (−₱18,383.75) — and it was two accounts, not the math. Players (410) and rounds per player were normal; stake size was not. Average bet hit ₱13.50 against ₱4.10–₱10.63 every other day, with 0 rounds at ₱500+ versus 0–2 elsewhere. BP1_bingoplusri8nof and BP1_bingoplusn08b08 alone placed 18.47% of the day's turnover. Maintenance records confirm no RTP or payout-formula change shipped that day.
  • 2026-09-17 carried the week. The lowest RTP of the seven (95.01%) produced ₱37,743.50 — 35.68% of all weekly GGR — on ordinary stakes (average bet ₱5.47, zero rounds at ₱500+).
  • Concentration is the exposure, not RTP. Two days decide the week's result; the other five sit in a narrow 95.07%–100.34% band on steady traffic (354–2415 actives all week). Watch single-account stake concentration.

  • Retention = that day's "Returned From Prior Day" count ÷ the prior day's total active players.
  • 2026-09-14 (the week's first day) is excluded — no prior day in this single-week window to measure against.
  • Day-over-day retention holds in a steady 9–11% band across the week, with no clear upward or downward drift — a single week isn't enough data to call this a trend either way.
  • Survival curve is built from all 647,219 order rows this week across all 9,535 players (not just new signups — see New Player & Churn Analysis for the acquisition-cohort view).
  • Just under half the roster (46.77%) plays past round 30, but it thins out fast after that: only 15.08% reach round 100, and just 0.62% (6 players) reach round 1,000+.
  • Status is the backend's playerStatus rule — active = a settled bet within the last 7 days — shown as of the date on the panel, which is after the report week. It is therefore a churn signal about W36's players, not a W36 in-window figure (as of the week's own cutoff every roster player had just bet, so that reading would be 100% active by construction). Coverage is complete: 760 of 975 come from the backend flag directly, and the remaining 215 are derived from settled orders using that same rule, validated at 100% agreement (0 mismatches across 1,413 backend rows). The shared order cache covers the full 7-day window with no gaps, so an absent bet is genuine inactivity rather than missing data.
  • On active days: the overwhelming majority — 869 players (89.13%) — only ever bet on a single calendar day this week; 86 (8.82%) returned on a 2nd day, and only 10 players (1.03%) logged bets on 4 or more separate days within the 7-day window.
  • Round volume and multi-day return are two very different things — a player can rack up hundreds of rounds in one sitting (see the survival curve) without ever coming back on a different day.

FindingsSep 14–20
The two platforms differ the same way on both measures: Bingo Plus has the higher D1 (8.40% against 6.79%) and the milder early experience (63.1% of players reaching 20 rounds already down, against 68.4%). Retention and the first-20 rounds move together here.
  • Bingo Plus: D1 8.40%, 63.1% of players who reached 20 rounds were already down, averaging -₱5.50 net on ₱205.52 of bet (D1 base 1,464 players)
  • Game Zone: D1 6.79%, 68.4% of players who reached 20 rounds were already down, averaging -₱2.56 net on ₱69.52 of bet (D1 base 5,599 players)
Two platforms ordered consistently is a correlation, not a cause -- and each is one point. It is consistent with the early experience driving return, which is what the numbers should be read against, not proof of it.

FindingsSep 14–20
Game Zone's 95.30% RTP is -4.76 pp against Bingo Plus's 100.06%, and the driver is within-tier payout — tiers that Bingo Plus also carries return less here.
  • blended RTP 95.30% against 100.06% for Bingo Plus — a gap of -4.76 pp
  • -1.43 pp of that is bet mix, -3.33 pp is within-tier payout (the two sum to the gap)
  • largest within-tier contributor — ₱2,000-₱10,000: 98.23% here against 103.78% on Bingo Plus (-5.56 pp) across 26.5% of bet
Mix and rate are not independent: a tier's share and its payout both move. This says which one moved more, not that the other is unchanged.

  • Bonus Trigger Round is real and material — 1,492 rounds (2.27% of volume) triggered a nonzero "other payout" on top of the base bet, contributing ₱215,680.00 of payout from only ₱17,790.00 of bet in those rounds.
  • That payout-to-bet ratio (1,212.37%) is expected, not an error: a Bonus Trigger Round's payout is driven by the feature outcome, not by the small base stake that triggered it, so per-category RTP is not comparable to the blended RTP.
  • Buy Feature rounds (223, 0.34%) carry a much larger average stake (₱154.71/round vs ₱10.06 for Normal Rounds) and actually run a healthier RTP (79.23%) than Normal Rounds (66.94%) this week.
  • Feature reconciliation: Normal Rounds (63,900) + Bonus Trigger Round (1,492) + Mission Feature (0) + Buy Feature (223) = 647,219 settled rounds. Total settled rounds = 647,219. Result: PASSED.
  • Bonus Trigger Round is identified by NORMAL_BET rows with a nonzero other-payout amount; Normal Rounds is NORMAL_BET with other-payout zero or blank; Buy Feature is the BUY_FEATURE bet type; Mission requires an explicit confirmed mission signal, which was not observed in any row this week.

Unlike the monthly report's version of this panel — pulled live from queryPageRtpAdjustRecord — this week's numbers come straight from the adjustType field already present on every settled order row, so no separate live pull was needed to reconstruct the type breakdown and reach figures. Only the two trigger-threshold configuration values above genuinely require that live endpoint and aren't available for this week.
  • DAILY and CUMULATIVE dominate (83.73% of all 19,684 events) and both run RTP above 283.89%: these are compensation events that push payout up once the rolling RTP drifts below a trigger threshold, and they're the same underlying mechanic behind the Bonus Trigger Round RTP outlier (1,279.98%) already flagged in the panel above.
  • DISCARD and REROLL events run close to or below 100% RTP and read as adjustments that were calculated but not fully paid out.
  • Adjust events touch only 3.23% of the week's bet volume but 9.33% of its payout — a small, engineered slice of rounds doing disproportionate work to hold the blended RTP near target — and 71.9% of the week's players hit at least one of them.

  • Each cell is one hour of one day. Blue means the hour ran below the 97% target (house-favourable); red means it ran above (player-favourable); near-neutral grey is within ±3 pp of target. Read the pattern, not any single cell — the useful question is whether hot hours cluster by time of day or by date, and here they do not: the red cells are scattered across all seven days and across the clock, which is what an unbiased game looks like.
  • Hourly RTP is a small-sample statistic and swings hard: across the coloured cells it runs from 76% to 149%, far wider than the weekly close. That range is sampling noise, not the game changing. Buckets holding fewer than 50 rounds (1 of them) are hatched rather than coloured — painting a confident red on a six-round hour would invent a pattern that is not there. 167 cells carry enough rounds to colour.
